newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber flat at close, Tokyo fall ignored.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber flat at close, Tokyo fall ignored.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market finished on a flat tone on Tuesday as players sat back ahead of a holiday while the sharp fall of the Tokyo market was largely a non-factor here, dealers said.

"I haven't seen that much impact from what happened in Japan because most people are out for the holidays," a trader said. "The fall in Tokyo was a bit of a surprise but the impact here was minimal. We'll see something the closer we get to the spot expiry next week," another dealer said. Tokyo rubber futures tumbled to a limit low due to the steep gains of the yen with key October contract down seven yen at 135.2.
"I heard another reason for the sharp fall in Tokyo was because some Thai players dumped a lot of rubber in the market," a dealer said.

But another dealer said the Thais were probably just liquidating their holdings because "most of them are in a short position." Traders said there was also market talk that the Thai government bought a few hundred tonnes of rubber.

Trading in the local market ahead of a holiday tomorrow was thin. At 0945 GMT, January/March RSS3 was seen at 117.00 U.S. cents a kg from 119.25 cents. Oct/December TSR20 was two U.S. cents down at 110.75 cents a kg.
